sentences.text: This small crocodyliform measured about one meter in total length, based on a skull roughly 20 centimeters long.
Its narrow snout featured wavy margins around the teeth, a unique dental arrangement.
The skull also displays an hourglass shape in the choanae, the nasal passage openings on the underside of the bone.
Unlike many relatives, it lacks antorbital and mandibular fenestrae and has a premaxilla bone extending backward to the fifth maxillary tooth.
The genus name Batrachomimus means "batrachian mimic" because the holotype was originally misidentified as a temnospondyl, a prehistoric amphibian resembling modern frogs and toads.
This name alludes to the evolutionary replacement of temnospondyls by crocodyliforms as dominant semi-aquatic predators during the Jurassic period.
The single species Batrachomimus pastosbonensis was described and named in 2013 by Felipe C. Montefeltro, Hans C. E. Larsson, Marco A. G. de França, and Max C. Langer.
Phylogenetic analysis places Batrachomimus as the most basal member of the family Paralligatoridae, a group that also includes the Cretaceous Asian genera Shamosuchus and Rugosuchus.
It lived during the Late Jurassic in the Pastos Bons Formation of northeastern Brazil.
Its time range spans the Oxfordian to the Kimmeridgian stages, between 161.5 and 149.2 million years ago.
